model: VT8650 Rooftop Unit and Heat Pump Controller
equipment_type: Rooftop unit controller (room thermostat, conventional or heat-pump RTUs)
applies_to: Viconics VT8000-series VT8650 room controllers for packaged rooftop units and heat pumps (up to 2 heating and 2 cooling stages), with economizer and indoor air quality options.
summary: The VT8650 is the rooftop unit and heat pump version of the Viconics VT8000 room controller. It is a BACnet application-specific controller (B-ASC) on BACnet MS/TP, with BACnet IP and Wi-Fi status objects for units set up through the Wi-Fi configuration web page. MV 119 Application selects rooftop or heat pump; the objects cover G/Y1/Y2/W1/W2-OB stage outputs, economizer and fresh-air limits, CO2-based IAQ control, supply and mixed air temperatures, and the common VT8000 display, Lua and ZigBee wireless sensor objects.
notes: Viconics is a Schneider Electric brand; the guide is published on veris.com.
Stage outputs BO 25-29 are G Fan, Y1, Y2, W1 and W2/OB Status; MV 117 sets the reversing valve to O or B for heat pump use.

Access follows the guide's generic property tables: AV, AO, BV, BO and MSV present values are commandable, CSVs are writable, and AI/MSI present values can only be written while Out_Of_Service is TRUE.
Wireless Device 1-20 objects only report data for ZigBee sensors paired to the controller.
Printed as in the guide: AV 42 default 78°F (21°C); AV 85 Cooling CPH max printed 4; MV 136 and MV 185 max printed 2 with three states.

integration.summary: Command occupancy with MV 10, mode with MV 16 and fan mode with MV 17, and write the occupied setpoints AV 39/AV 40. Read AV 100 room temperature, MI 33 effective occupancy, MV 112 control status, the G fan output BO 25 and the fan lock alarm BV 39. Write at priorities 4-16 for live control; avoid 1-3.

integration.enable: No enable switch is needed. The BMS writes MV 10 Occupancy Command (1 = Loc. occ, the controller decides locally; 2 = Occupied; 3 = Unoccupied) and MV 16 System Mode. MV 110 Occupancy Source chooses whether local occupancy follows motion, the schedule or a mix.
integration.remote_sensors: The guide has no BMS-written room temperature object: MV 145 Room Temperature Sensor selects the wired, internal or one of 20 paired ZigBee wireless sensors, and MI 309 shows which one is in use. Writing an AI present value only works with Out_Of_Service set TRUE.
setup: The Device Object_Identifier and Object_Name are writable; no default device instance is printed in the guide.
BACnet MS/TP baud rate is MV 8 (9600, 19200, 38400, 57600, 76800, 115200 or Auto; default Auto). Max_Master is writable, 0-127, default 127.
MI 317 shows whether BACnet IP is enabled; it is set from the BACnet/IP page of the Wi-Fi configuration web page.
COV subscriptions are supported (DS-COV-B), along with an internal schedule (SCHED-I-B) and time synchronization.
gotchas: Priorities 1-3 are stored in EEPROM and lock the value at the thermostat, even after a power cycle, until it is released at the same priority or factory defaults are restored. Use them only for fixed configuration.
Priorities 4-16 are held in RAM and are lost on a power cycle, so the BMS has to write them again after the controller restarts.
The relinquish default (priority 17) is the value the occupant changes at the thermostat, which is kept through power cycles. Writes at 4-16 override local changes to setpoints and modes.
The controller does not support segmented requests or responses; keep Read Property Multiple requests small.
MV 119 Application, the stage counts (AV 75, AV 87) and MV 117 reversing valve setting are commissioning settings; do not write them cyclically.
